comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that dual targeting (CCA) induces robust MG proliferation without damage stimulus. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis (C45-C52, C102), while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'convincing' evidence and note improved imaging quality. Complete agreement on this central claim.

Perfect alignment on self-limiting proliferation. Both accept the temporal dynamics (C53-C57), EdU/BrdU double-labeling (C58-C59), and clonal analysis (C60-C61) showing single division. Peer reviewers note satisfactory responses to previous concerns and do not challenge methodology or interpretation.

Complete agreement on temporal dynamics of cyclin D1 and p27Kip1 expression (C62-C67, C113-C115). Both accept the mechanistic explanation for self-limiting proliferation. Peer reviewers explicitly note acceptance of FISH and scRNA-seq data supporting these molecular findings.

Both support IFN pathway suppression findings (C68, C70-C71, C118-C121) from scRNA-seq. OpenEval notes mechanistic link remains speculative, while peer reviewer explicitly highlights this as an interesting finding that 'may contribute to induced retinal regeneration.' Agreement on data, with peer review more accepting of mechanistic interpretation.

Complete agreement on Stat3 divergent regulation (C72-C73, C123-C126). Both accept scRNA-seq findings and interpretation linking Stat3 to proliferation without neurogenesis. OpenEval suggests functional validation would strengthen claims, but peer reviewers do not raise this concern.

Both support transient glial gene suppression and recovery (C7-C9, C37, C76-C80). OpenEval emphasizes multiple orthogonal methods, while peer reviewers note improved imaging quality and acceptance of FISH/scRNA-seq data. Agreement on temporal dynamics and recovery of glial identity.

Both support MG retention of glial identity (C10, C38-C39, C81, C93-C94, C132). OpenEval provides detailed quantification showing preserved MG numbers, while peer reviewers affirm approach works 'without disrupting retinal structure or function.' Complete agreement on glial fate maintenance.

Both support low-level neuronal marker expression (C11-C12, C40, C83-C88). OpenEval notes appropriate caution about 'latent neurogenic potential' being speculative, while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge after improved imaging quality. Agreement on data with OpenEval more explicit about interpretive limitations.

Strong agreement on safety profile (C13, C41-C42, C89-C92, C95-C97, C111, C117). Both accept ERG, optomotor, histology, and TUNEL data showing no adverse effects at 1 year. Peer reviewers explicitly state approach works 'without disrupting retinal structure or function.' OpenEval notes TUNEL limitation acknowledged by authors.

Both support the negative finding that CCA alone is insufficient for neurogenesis (C74-C75, C130-C131). OpenEval notes mechanistic explanation is speculative, while peer reviewers accept the conclusion and note improved interpretation removing rod gene references. Agreement on lack of robust neurogenic reprogramming.

Perfect agreement on rod gene contamination interpretation (C127-C129). Both accept that rod-MG enrichment results from ambient contamination rather than genuine reprogramming. Peer reviewer explicitly praises 'nuanced interpretation' and control experiments addressing this confound.

Both accept MG-specific targeting via GFAP promoter (C43-C44). OpenEval emphasizes these as critical methodological controls, while peer reviewers implicitly accept specificity by not raising concerns about off-target expression. Agreement on targeting specificity.

OpenEval rates age-dependent proliferation kinetics explanation (C103-C106) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct validation of AAV transduction efficiency. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these speculative mechanistic claims about age effects.

OpenEval rates mechanisms for self-limiting proliferation (C112, C115-C116) as UNCERTAIN, noting AAV dilution and Btg2 upregulation are speculative without direct measurement. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these mechanistic hypotheses, though C115 overlaps with accepted temporal dynamics in R8.

OpenEval supports morphological observations of rare Sox9-negative cells (C82) as descriptive data, appropriately noting morphology alone insufficient for neuronal identity. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing this morphological claim.

OpenEval supports background/rationale claims (C1-C4, C14-C34) as well-cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

Both support translational potential and future directions (C136-C137 overlap). OpenEval notes these are speculative proposals based on findings, while peer reviewers affirm 'promising approach' for regenerative therapies and 'valuable tool for combinatorial therapies.' Agreement on forward-looking implications, though OpenEval also includes broader literature contextualization (C98-C101, C107-C108, C120, C122, C133) not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.
